title: Great Migration Facts and Numbers
excerpt: How many animals take part in the Great Migration, how far do they walk, and why? Facts and figures with honest caveats.
body:
The Great Migration is often described as one of the greatest wildlife spectacles on earth. Here are some facts.

## How many animals?

Estimates commonly cited are around 1.3 to 1.5 million wildebeest, plus hundreds of thousands of zebras and gazelles. Counts vary by year and method.

## How far?

The herds move in a circular route of several hundred kilometres per year through the Serengeti and Masai Mara.

## Why?

They follow rain and fresh grass. The southern plains have nutrient-rich grass during the rains, which is important for calving.

## Calving

A large proportion of calves is born within a few weeks, which overwhelms predators. See [Ndutu](/blog/ndutu-calving-season/).

## Zebras and wildebeest

Zebras and wildebeest graze on different parts of the grass, so they complement each other.

## Predators

Lions, hyenas, cheetahs, leopards and crocodiles depend on the herds.

## A protected ecosystem

The migration exists because the Serengeti–Mara ecosystem is protected across borders. See [conservation in Tanzania](/blog/conservation-in-tanzania/).
